title: Battery Charging
summary: OSHA's construction battery standard sets rules for battery areas and charging. This talk covers ventilation, protective gear, quick drench facilities, and where and how to charge.
talking_points: Place unsealed batteries in enclosed spaces with outside vents or in well-ventilated areas so fumes, gases and electrolyte spray do not reach other spaces.
Ventilation must help gases spread out and keep an explosive mixture from building up.
Battery racks and trays must be sturdy and treated to resist damage from electrolyte.
Floors in battery areas must be acid-resistant or have a protective coating.
Workers who handle acids or batteries must have face shields, aprons and rubber gloves available.
Quick drenching facilities for the eyes and body must be within 25 feet of battery handling areas.
Keep spill response and fire suppression equipment available for electrolyte incidents.
Charge batteries only in designated locations. Protect charging equipment from vehicle damage and keep vent caps in place during charging.
site_hazards_to_check: Battery storage or charging in a closed space with poor ventilation
Damaged, corroded or untreated battery racks and trays
No eyewash or drench facility within 25 feet of the battery area
Missing face shield, apron or rubber gloves
Charging done outside a designated area, or chargers exposed to vehicle traffic
Vent caps missing or damaged on batteries being charged
discussion_questions: Where is our designated battery charging area, and why is it there?
Where is the nearest eye and body drench station to the batteries?
What would you do if electrolyte spilled or sprayed during charging?

attribution.notice: Adapted from 29 CFR 1926.441, Batteries and battery charging. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Content matches 29 CFR 1926.441(a)-(b) as summarized in the source (unsealed batteries ventilated, racks/trays treated, acid-resistant floors, face shield/apron/rubber gloves, drench within 25 ft, spill and fire equipment, designated charging area, protect chargers from vehicles, vent caps in place). Citation is a correct 1926 section.

Source note: the raw file is a condensed summary, not verbatim (only paragraphs a-b). Non-blocking: the talk omits hydrogen-ignition precautions (no smoking, open flame, or sparks near charging) that are standard practice but not in 1926.441; consider adding from a further source.
Public domain, osha.gov. No UK wording.
